output.methodChoice: Provenance check of the initial claims, then Kepner-Tregoe is/is-not on per-cell timing (X7), then competing-hypotheses weighing with storage metrics (X2).
output.brief: Don't roll back gateway 5.8. The regression comes from the 2 Nov storage compaction tuning change, not the gateway. In 11 cells the fleet config push (compaction threads raised from 2 to 6) landed at about 23:40. Within minutes, disk use jumped from 41% to 97% and node-side GET time went from 61 ms to 262 ms. p99 crossed 150 ms 5–10 minutes after each push, regardless of when 5.8 arrived. One cell (aps-3) got 5.8 but skipped the push, and its p99 stayed at about 94 ms. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. A rollback would drop the signature security fix (audit deadline 30 Nov) and would not fix latency. Network and traffic growth don't fit the timing. Next steps: revert the tuning in one cell, watch p99 and backlog, then extend it. Also watch the compaction backlog, which was 11.2% on 2 Nov against the roughly 15% trouble point, and handle it by other means. Do not pause compaction, because that risks disk-full. Hold off on throttling Orrin until the 10 Nov attribution report. The gateway CPU profiling is optional follow-up. Confidence is high. The remaining uncertainty is what drove the backlog growth.
